summary: Gin Ling Liu is a scholar in Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Hong Kong, where she was supervised by Jing Yin, and also studied under the traditional teacher Hsing Yun (all attested 2008).

Giovanni Gentile (1875–1944) was an Italian philosopher who studied at the Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa and the universities of Pisa and Florence. He held professorships at Palermo, Pisa, and Sapienza University of Rome, and served as director of the Scuola Normale Superiore.

Giovanni Vacca (1872–1953) was an Italian scholar of sinology, history, and archaeology. He earned his doctorate at the University of Genoa and studied at Florence, later lecturing at Florence and holding chairs in East Asian subjects at Sapienza University of Rome (1911–1948).

Giovanni Verardi (born 1947) is a scholar of archaeology, history, and Buddhist studies who studied at the universities of Allahabad, Banaras Hindu, and Gorakhpur. His academic posts include Ca' Foscari University, Bologna, and a professorship at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (1988–1993).

Girindrasekhar Bose (1887–1953) was an Indian scholar who studied at Presidency University, Medical College Kolkata, and the University of Calcutta. He was Professor of Experimental Psychology at the University of Calcutta (1917–1949) and president of the Indian Psychoanalytic Society (1922–1953).

Gisela Emma Full is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at the universities of Würzburg and Münster. In 2013, she was attested as a research fellow at European University Viadrina and the Samueli Institute.

Gisela Freund (1920–2023) was an archaeologist who studied at the German University of Prague (~1939–1944). She served as Head of the Department of Prehistory at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg from approximately 1974 to 1987.

Gisho Nakano (1891–1977) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu and obtained a doctorate from Kyushu University. He held professorships at Peking University and Koyasan University, where he also served as president.
Giti Dutt is an archaeology and history researcher. As attested in 2026, she is a PhD student at the Australian National University studying under the doctoral supervision of Assa Doron.
Giuliana Martini is a scholar in Buddhist studies who held posts at Kyoto University and the Italian School of East Asian Studies in 2010.

Giuseppe Bardelli (1815–1865) was an Italian scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied under Giuseppe Mezzofanti, Eugène Burnouf, and Stanislas Julien, and served as a lecturer in Coptic and Sanskrit at the University of Pisa (~1845–1865).
Giuseppe Mezzofanti (1774–1849) studied at the University of Bologna from approximately 1786 to 1797 and subsequently held a post there from around 1797 to 1831.

Giuseppe Tucci (1894–1984) was an Italian scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and archaeology who studied at Sapienza University of Rome and Visva-Bharati University. He became a professor at Sapienza and served as president of the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East.

Giuseppe Vignato is a scholar of archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He pursued doctoral studies at Peking University under teachers including Angela Falco Howard, Chongfeng Li, Su Bai, and Shichang Ma, later holding an academic post there (attested 2017).

Giyu Nishi (1897–1993) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Taiken Kimura, Sylvain Lévi, and Junjirō Takakusu, among others. He was an assistant at the University of Tokyo (1926) and became a professor at Toyo University (1927).

Glenn H. Mullin (born 1949) is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under numerous traditional teachers, including the 14th Dalai Lama, Ling Rinpoche, and Trijang Rinpoche, and founded the Mystical Arts of Tibet in 1984.
Glenn Wallis is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under academic teacher Masatoshi Nagatomi and traditional teacher Ross Bolleter.
Gnanawimala Chandima is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara under Uma Shankar Vyas.

Godabarish Mishra (1886–1956) was an Indian scholar in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Ravenshaw College and the University of Calcutta, worked as a teacher and headmaster, and served as Director at the University of Madras.

Gombojab Tsybikov (1873–1930) was a scholar of Tibetology and Central Asian studies. He studied at Tomsk State University and Saint Petersburg State University, later serving as a lecturer and professor at the Oriental Institute and Far Eastern Federal University in Vladivostok (~1902–1917).
